h: Guild Wheel Rides and Riverside Steam
p: Smaller wildlife parks like Wild Discovery are ideal for families with younger kids who might be overwhelmed by a big zoo. It's a manageable size, so you can wander at a relaxed pace, linger with the animals that catch your eye, and not worry about missing anything. Encourage the kids to ask questions if staff are around; they're often happy to share facts about the animals.

Little ones with short attention spans do best with a plan: pick three animals they're desperate to see, find those first, and treat everything else as a bonus. Pop a waterproof in the bag regardless of the forecast, because Lancashire rarely keeps its promises, and keep a snack back for the drive home.

Preston has a few surprises up its sleeve for families. The Guild Wheel is a 21-mile cycling and walking route that loops around the city, taking in riverside paths, parks and countryside. You don't have to do the whole thing; even a short stretch along the River Ribble is a great way to stretch your legs.

Down by Preston Docks, the Ribble Steam Railway runs heritage trains alongside the marina and has a museum packed with locomotives, ideal for little train fans. The marina itself is a pleasant spot for a stroll and a bite to eat. Preston is also famous for the Preston Guild, a celebration held only once every 20 years, with the last one in 2012 and the next due in 2032. It's a real once-in-a-generation event, so pencil it in if you fancy planning way, way ahead.

Preston was only granted city status in 2002 as part of Queen Elizabeth II's Golden Jubilee celebrations, which surprises plenty of people given its long history as a busy Lancashire market and mill town.
